column1: # Game profile of Cuphead (Switch, base game v0 + update 1.3.7 = v655360, with The Delicious Last Course as DLC index 1). Plays on the Mac and on the iPhone

# Unity 2017.4.9f1 (IL2CPP), SDK 5.5.0 (the oldest so far), NVN API 53.313: the shaders are Shader objects in the AssetBundles of StreamingAssets and the player's serialized files (read by shader_split.py through unityfs.py).
# Unity 2017.4's serialized and Shader formats and the rewriter's jump-table form were found by armyja on this game (GitHub pull requests #1 and #2)

# Game name: only a label for profile listings and the Mac window title; the iOS app name is the game name in the base NSP, and the bundle ID comes from the base game title ID (build_ipa.sh / NSP script)
# only the merged 1.3.7 copy is extracted
# load order as on Horizon: main, subsdk*, sdk (subsdk0 = NintendoSDK_movie)
# The NPDM declares no system resource, so the game has no virtual address memory: Unity sets a heap of the application pool − used memory (3.12 GB) and allocates from it.
# The block is 256 MB in front + 256 MB alias region + 256 MB stack region + 3.25 GB heap region
# the rewritten modules take 80 MB (main 59.9, sdk 12.7, subsdk0 7.3), more than the default 64 MB of used memory: with 64 MB the heap request plus the modules exceeds the pool and SetHeapSize fails
# the game calls nvnDeviceSetDepthMode with near = 0 (its log: "this run needs ... depth near=0"): the pipeline bases made before it runs are made for that mode
# ---- Shader split (shader_split.py; Unity Shader objects, read by unityfs.py) ----
